# Argus – Hidden Camera Detector

> Argus – Hidden Camera Detector is an iPhone app (iOS 16 or later, 26 languages) that finds hidden cameras and trackers in hotel rooms, Airbnbs, rentals and changing rooms with four on-device checks: a Wi-Fi scan for the ports cameras stream on, a camera finder with Lens and Infrared modes, a Bluetooth scan that recognises item trackers and walks you to them, and a magnet check for electronics hidden inside objects. It is made by Roman Hadiiev, App Store ID 6790475588.

Key facts:

- Free, with no scan limit, no account, no ads and no trial that turns into a charge: the camera finder's Lens mode; the Wi-Fi scan, which shows how many devices share the Wi-Fi with you and how many are new since recent scans, and warns when a device on the network could be a hidden camera; the Bluetooth scan, which counts possible trackers and the devices close to you; and Find it, which walks you to a possible tracker by its live signal.
- Wi-Fi device names: Argus reads the names, models and kinds devices announce on the network (Bonjour: AirPlay, Chromecast, printers, HomeKit, smart-home devices) and, on iOS 27, names a device's maker from its hardware (MAC) address. A device from a camera maker (Hikvision, Dahua, Ezviz, Wyze, Ring, Reolink) is flagged as a possible camera even when no camera port answers, since cloud cameras open none; a device that announces itself as a HomeKit camera or doorbell or as an RTSP video service is rated a likely camera; routers and gateways from makers that build no cameras, and devices that announce a non-camera kind, are set aside. A maker is a hint, never a verdict.
- Argus Pro, an optional weekly or yearly subscription, shows which device it is. For Wi-Fi devices: the name, model and maker (from what the device announces and, on iOS 27, its MAC address); the IP address; the camera ports that answered (RTSP 554 and 8554, ONVIF 8899 and 2020, Dahua 37777, XMEye 34567, V380 8800/9800, Ezviz, Hikvision 8000, Reolink 9000 and the web ports); the device's own reply; a camera rating with the reason; and which devices are new since the last scan. For Bluetooth devices: name or maker, including many devices that send no name, signal strength, which kind of tracker a tracker looks like, and Find it for any device. Pro also adds Infrared mode, which spots the light of night-vision cameras, and the magnet check.
- Method: Argus combines network scanning with lens and infrared inspection instead of relying on the phone's magnetometer alone, which a USENIX Security 2023 study of detector apps found to be of little help. The magnetometer is used only for a close-range check of one object.
- Bluetooth answer: when a scan ends, possible trackers come first, then how many devices are close to you (probably in this room; some may be your own), and the rest grouped by kind. Trackers recognised: Tile, Samsung SmartTag, Chipolo, Pebblebee and Google Find Hub tags. For AirTags, the iPhone also alerts its owner itself.
- Privacy: no account and no Argus server. Scan results, camera frames and sensor readings are processed on the iPhone and never uploaded; only the subscription receipt (with Apple's note of whether the install came from one of Argus's Apple Search Ads ads: campaign, ad group and keyword, no advertising identifier), crash and error reports and usage counts leave the phone, never a device name, address or sensor reading. No ads, no advertising identifier, no cross-app tracking.
- Four checks because each method has a blind spot: a switched-off camera is not on the Wi-Fi but its lens still glints; a camera on its own SIM is not on the network but its night-vision light can show in Infrared mode. No app can promise to find every device.
- Argus is not related to "Argus: AntiSpy Camera Sweep", which is by a different developer, nor to Reolink Argus security cameras.

- [Is that unknown device on the Wi-Fi a hidden camera?](https://tatrom.github.io/unknown-device-on-wifi-hidden-camera-iphone/): the ports that give a camera away, how Argus names devices and their makers, and how to check every device on the network
- [Hidden camera detector apps for iPhone, compared (2026)](https://tatrom.github.io/hidden-camera-detector-apps-iphone-compared/): nine apps compared by method (Wi-Fi camera-port check, lens, infrared, Bluetooth trackers, magnetometer) and what each keeps free, from their own App Store pages
